title: The potassium gate opens
hook: Predict the next step, then trace the signal.

knows: Neurons have membranes and communicate using electrical and chemical signals.
doesNotKnow: During the usual falling phase, potassium leaves the neuron through open potassium channels, helping bring the membrane potential back down.

misconception: Neuronal signals and chemical synapses involve no ion movement.
objective: Explain the specified step of neuronal signaling under the stated conditions.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: During the falling phase of a typical neuronal action potential, voltage-gated potassium channels open. In which direction is the net potassium movement? During the usual falling phase, potassium leaves the neuron through open potassium channels, helping bring the membrane potential back down.
The diagrams are schematic, show only selected particles or steps, and do not represent actual particle trajectories or scale.

Recall: When positive charge moves into a cell, with other currents neglected, what happens to the inside voltage? Net entry of positive charge makes the inside less negative in this simplified model.
